elements.label: text

elements.char: ntroduction
elements.label: text

elements.char: Many important problems across different fields of economics require solving dynamic
elements.label: text

elements.char: stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) or optimal decision-making problems. Numeri-
elements.label: text

elements.char: cal dynamic programming (DP) is a typical method to solve such problems by formu-
elements.label: text

elements.char: lating them as Bellman equation (Bellman (1957)) and then solving them with value
elements.label: text

elements.char: function iteration (or some accelerating methods like policy function iteration) or time
elements.label: text

elements.char: iteration.
elements.label: text

elements.char: However, implementing numerical DP faces challenging problems such as
elements.label: text

elements.char: time-consuming high-dimensional integration, keeping the shape properties of the
elements.label: text

elements.char: value/policy function approximation (Cai and Judd (2013, 2015)), choosing appropri-
elements.label: text

elements.char: ate approximation domains, avoiding possible nonconvergence because of accumu-
elements.label: text

elements.char: lated approximation errors, and dealing with the kinks from inequality constraints that
elements.label: text

elements.char: occasionally bind. Choosing a good approximation can be particularly challenging for
elements.label: text

elements.char: multidimensional dynamic stochastic problems where the domain of state variables ex-
elements.label: text

elements.char: pands quickly over time, while a wider domain requires a higher degree approximation.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Its implementation for high-dimensional problems is very time-consuming even if we
elements.label: text

elements.char: take advantage of recent innovations, such as parallel dynamic programming methods
elements.label: text

elements.char: (Cai, Judd, Thain, and Wright (2015b)) in a supercomputer or a computational grid.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Because of these challenges it is common in applied economics to rely on methods
elements.label: text

elements.char: other than numerical DP and sacrifice accuracy of results for the greater ease of nu-
elements.label: text

elements.char: merical implementation. The most common method is log-linearization; Magill (1977)
elements.label: text

elements.char: introduced linearization methods for dynamic stochastic models to economics. Linear
elements.label: text

elements.char: (and log-linear) approximations produce decision rules that depend only on the state
elements.label: text

elements.char: of a deterministic dynamical system. They are also called certainty-equivalent approxi-
elements.label: text

elements.char: mations because they do not depend on the variance of any random variable. Because
elements.label: text

elements.char: of its local nature, log-linearization often fails to give a good solution on states that are
elements.label: text

elements.char: not near the steady state.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Moreover, perturbation methods are unsuitable for problems
elements.label: text

elements.char: with inequality constraints.
elements.label: text

elements.char: This paper introduces a new method for solving dynamic problems in economics
elements.label: text

elements.char: that we call the nonlinear certainty-equivalent (NLCEQ) approximation method. Ap-
elements.label: text

elements.char: plication of certainty-equivalent approximations goes back to Simon (1956) and Theil
elements.label: text

elements.char: (1957), who suggested solving dynamic programming problems with quadratic objec-
elements.label: text

elements.char: tives and linear transition laws by optimizing under perfect foresight, and then using
elements.label: text

elements.char: optimal deterministic forecasts for approximating unknown future values. They also
elements.label: text

elements.char: demonstrated that for some stochastic control problems, the certainty-equivalent ap-
elements.label: text

elements.char: proximation is the exact solution for the optimal decision rules.
elements.label: text

elements.char: The NLCEQ method
elements.label: text

elements.char: is a natural extension of the idea of a certainty equivalent in that it solves for a nonlin-
elements.label: text

elements.char: For a detailed discussion of these methods, see Judd (1998), Bertsekas (2005, 2007), Rust (2008), and Cai
elements.label: text

elements.char: and Judd (2014).
elements.label: text

elements.char: For more detailed discussion of perturbation methods in economics, see Gaspar and Judd (1997), Jin
elements.label: text

elements.char: and Judd (2002), Schmitt-Grohe and Uribe (2004), Fernandez-Villaverde and Rubio-Ramirez (2006), Kim,
elements.label: text

elements.char: Kim, Schaumburg, and Sims (2008), and Den Haan and De Wind (2012).
